props.gloss_en: one who prayed, entered the synagogue and found the congregation praying: if he can introduce something new in it, he prays again
and if not, he does not pray again

had he taught us the first [ruling], [one would say] that holds of individual and individual or congregation and congregation, but an individual vis-a-vis the congregation is as one who has not prayed -- so he taught us [this one]
and had he taught us here, [one would say] it is because he had not begun it, but there, where he had begun it, say not -- [both are] necessary
Rav Huna: one who enters the synagogue and finds the congregation praying -- if he can begin and finish before the prayer leader reaches 'Modim', he prays; if not, he does not
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: if he can begin and finish before the prayer leader reaches 'Kedusha', he prays; if not, he does not
what do they dispute? whether an individual says kedusha
one master holds: an individual says kedusha
and the other master holds: an individual does not say kedusha
from where that an individual does not say kedusha? as it is said: 'and I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel' (Lev 22:32)
any matter of sanctity shall not be [said] with fewer than ten
and according to all, at any rate, one does not interrupt [his prayer]
one does not interrupt for anything except 'May His great name be blessed'
for even one engaged in the Work of the Chariot stops [for it]
the halakha follows him [the view Rav Dimi reported] on interrupting for 'May His great name be blessed' -- DENIED by the stam: ולית הלכתא כוותיה
